questions.question: National Sports Day of India is celebrated on 29 August every year in honour of which sportsperson?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Major Dhyan Chand Singh.**__

 
• **National Sports Day** of **India **is celebrated on** 29 August **every year to commemorate the** birth anniversary of hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand.**
 
• The **President **gives away** sport-related awards** such as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Arjuna Award and Dronacharya Award** on this day at the** Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi, India.**
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand** was known for his extraordinary goal-scoring capabilities. Known as the **Wizard **or the** Magician **of hockey for his** superb ball control. Major Dhyan Chand** played internationally from **1926 to 1949.**
 
• He won three **Olympic gold medals** in field hockey in the following events:
 
 
• **1928 Amsterdam **
 
• **1932 Los Angeles **
 
• **1936 Berlin **
 
 
 
• His influence and talent extended beyond his personal Olympic victories, as** India won the field hockey** event in** seven out of eight Olympics from 1928 to 1964.**
 
• He scored **570 goals in 185 matches** according to his **autobiography, Goal.**
 
• The Government of India **awarded Major Dhyan Chand** India's third highest civilian honour of Padma Bhushan in 1956.
 
• Government of India has issued a commemorative** postage stamp and a First Day Cover** in honour of Dhyan Chand. He remains the **only Indian hockey player **to have a **stamp in his honour.**
 
• The** National Stadium, Delhi **was renamed** Dhyan Chand National Stadium in 2002 **in his honour.

questions.question: Independence Day is celebrated every year in Pakistan on ________.
questions.solution:

__

• Independence Day commemorates the day when Pakistan gained **independence from British rule in 1947**.
 
• It is a national holiday in Pakistan, marked by flag-raising ceremonies, parades, cultural events, and patriotic displays.
 
• On this day, the national flag is hoisted on public and private buildings, and special prayers are offered for the prosperity and development of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pakistan was created as a result of the **Pakistan Movement led by the All-India Muslim League** under the leadership of **Muhammad Ali Jinnah**.
 
• The movement sought a separate nation for Muslims in the north-western and eastern zones of British India.
 
• The partition of India and Pakistan led to mass migrations and significant upheaval, impacting millions of lives.
 
• Independence Day is observed with great zeal and enthusiasm across Pakistan, highlighting the country's cultural heritage and national pride.
 
• In **Islamabad, the capital city**, the main celebrations are held at the Presidential and Parliament buildings, where the President and Prime Minister deliver speeches.

questions.question: When did the infamous Jallianwala Bagh incident take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13 April 1919.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **infamous Jallianwala Bagh** incident took place on **Sunday, April 13, 1919.**
 
• It was a** tragic incident **where British troops under the command of **General Reginald Dyer** fired upon a crowd of** unarmed Indian civilians** who had gathered for a peaceful protest against the arrest of two nationalist leaders.
 
• The incident resulted in the deaths of at least **379 people** and injured over a thousand others.
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre was a turning point in** India's struggle for independence** and led to widespread protests and outrage against British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Jallianwala Bagh is a **public garden l**ocated in** Amritsar, Punjab, India.**
 
• The incident is also known as the** Amritsar Massacre or the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.**
 
• General Dyer's actions were widely **condemned,** and he was eventually **relieved of his command** and forced to retire from the army.
 
• The incident led to the formation of the **Non-Cooperation Movement**, a major civil disobedience campaign led by Mahatma Gandhi, which played a significant role in India's struggle for independence.
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh site has been preserved as a** national monument **and serves as a reminder of the sacrifices made by the** Indian freedom fighters** in their struggle against British rule.

questions.question: International Day of Non-violence is observed on ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thu Oct 02 2025 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The International Day of Non-Violence is observed on **October 2nd** each year.
 
• This date was chosen to honor the birthday of **Mahatma Gandhi**, the leader of the Indian independence movement and a pioneer of the philosophy and strategy of non-violence.
 
• The day was established by the United Nations General Assembly in **2007**.
 
• The resolution for the International Day of Non-Violence was co-sponsored by **140 countries**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**:

 
 
• Born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, India.
 
• Known for his principles of **Satyagraha** (truth and non-violence).
 
• Played a crucial role in India's struggle for independence from British rule.
 
• Assassinated on January 30, 1948, in New Delhi, India.
 
 
 
• **Non-Violence**:
 
 
• A philosophy and strategy for social change that rejects the use of violence.
 
• Prominent non-violent leaders include Martin Luther King Jr., Nelson Mandela, and Cesar Chavez.
 
• Non-violence is also a principle in various religious traditions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, and Christianity.
 
 
 
• **United Nations General Assembly**:
 
 
• One of the six principal organs of the United Nations.
 
• Comprises all 193 member states of the UN.
 
• Responsible for making important decisions on peace and security, admission of new members, and budgetary matters.
 
• Resolutions adopted by the General Assembly are non-binding but carry significant moral weight.
 
 
 
• **Global Observances**:
 
 
• International days are occasions to educate the public on issues of concern.
 
• They mobilize political will and resources to address global problems.
 
• Examples include International Women's Day (March 8), World Health Day (April 7), and International Day of Peace (September 21).

questions.question: In India, Teachers' Day is celebrated annually on September 5 to mark the birthday of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Teachers' Day in India is celebrated on September 5 annually to honor the birth anniversary of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.
 
• Dr. Radhakrishnan was a renowned philosopher, scholar, and educator who served as the first Vice President and the second President of India.
 
• He was an advocate for education and a prominent figure in the academic field, contributing significantly to the education sector in India.
 
• The tradition of celebrating Teachers' Day began in 1962 when Dr. Radhakrishnan became the President of India and suggested that his birthday be celebrated as Teachers' Day to recognize the contributions of teachers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan**

 
 
• Born on September 5, 1888, in a small town of Tiruttani in Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• He was a distinguished scholar and academic who authored several books on philosophy and religion.
 
• Dr. Radhakrishnan was awarded several prestigious honors, including the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1954.
 
• He played a key role in shaping India's educational policies and institutions during his tenure as an academician and a statesman.
 
 
 
• **Teachers' Day**
 
 
• Teachers' Day is a special day dedicated to honoring and appreciating teachers for their contribution to education and society.
 
• It is celebrated in various countries around the world, often on different dates.
 
• In India, Teachers' Day is marked by various events and activities organized in schools and educational institutions to acknowledge the hard work and dedication of teachers.
 
• Students often express their gratitude to their teachers through cards, gifts, and special performances on this day.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Education**
 
 
• Education is essential for the overall development of individuals and societies.
 
• It empowers people with knowledge, skills, and values necessary for personal growth and social progress.
 
• Teachers play a crucial role in imparting education and shaping the future of students by providing guidance, support, and inspiration.
 
• Recognizing and celebrating the contributions of teachers is important to highlight the value of education and encourage a culture of respect for educators.

questions.question: The Third Battle of Panipat took place in ___________.

• The Third Battle of Panipat took place on January 14, 1761, between the Marathas and the Afghan invader Ahmad Shah Durrani.
 
• The battle was fought near the city of Panipat, which is now in the Indian state of Haryana.
 
• The Marathas were led by Sadashivrao Bhau, who was supported by other prominent leaders like Vishwasrao, the son of Peshwa Baji Rao I, and Ibrahim Khan Gardi.

questions.question: Republic Day in India is celebrated to commemorate:

options.text: the day when the Constituent Assembly was formed.
the date on which the Constitution of India came into effect.
the day when the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the date on which the Constitution of India came into effect.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Republic Day** in India is **celebrated to commemorate **the date on which the **Constitution of India came into effect,** transforming India into a newly formed republic. 
 
• This significant **event took place on January 26, 1950**
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949, but it came into effect on January 26, 1950.
 
• This date was chosen to honour the declaration of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) in 1930.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constituent Assembly was constituted in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan.
 
 
• Members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies.
 
• After the partition of India, the number of members of the Constituent Assembly came to 299, of whom 284 were actually present 
 
• It held its first meeting on December 9, 1946.
 
• The Constituent Assembly finalized the Constitution in two years, eleven months, and eighteen days.
 
• Objective Resolution was moved in the first session of the Constituent Assembly i.e. on 13 December 1946 by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question: On which of the following dates does India celebrate its Constitution Day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26th November**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Constitution Day is also known as **Samvidhan Divas** in India.
 
• It is observed on **26th November every year** to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949**, and it came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• On 19th November 2015, the Government of India declared 26th November as Constitution Day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitution of India**

 
 
• The Constitution of India is the supreme law of India.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• It is the longest written constitution of any country on earth.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is regarded as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Constitution**
 
 
• **Federal Structure:** The Constitution provides for a federal system of government with a division of powers between the central and state governments.
 
• **Parliamentary System:** It adopts a parliamentary system of government where the executive is responsible to the legislature.
 
• **Fundamental Rights:** It guarantees fundamental rights to all citizens, which include the right to equality, freedom, and protection against discrimination.
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:** These are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, aimed at creating social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• **Secular State:** The Constitution declares India to be a secular state, meaning that it does not favor any religion and allows individuals to practice any religion of their choice.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Constitution Day**
 
 
• Constitution Day is celebrated to honor and remember the importance of the Constitution and its framers.

questions.question: ________ is mainly celebrated by Maharashtrians as New Year's Day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gudi Padwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gudi Padwa:**

 
 
• Gudi Padwa is the Marathi New Year, celebrated primarily in Maharashtra and by Konkani Hindus.
 
• It falls on the first day of the Chaitra month, according to the Hindu lunisolar calendar, typically in March or April.
 
• The festival marks the beginning of the new year and the arrival of spring.
 
• A "Gudi" (a decorated bamboo stick) is raised outside homes, symbolizing victory and prosperity.
 
• It is a time for festive meals, colorful decorations, and celebrating new beginnings.
 
• It is considered an extremely auspicious time, for new ventures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ugadi:**

 
 
• Ugadi is the New Year's Day for the people of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.
 
• It also falls on the first day of the Chaitra month.
 
• Like Gudi Padwa, it signifies the start of a new lunar year.
 
• It is celebrated with colorful decorations, special dishes, and religious observances.
 
• The creation of a special pachadi, which is a dish that contains all six tastes, is a very important part of the celebration.
 
 
 
• **Pongal:**
 
 
• Pongal is a harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It typically occurs in mid-January.
 
• It is a four-day festival dedicated to thanking the Sun God for a bountiful harvest.
 
• The festival involves preparing a dish called "Pongal" (sweet rice), decorating homes, and honoring cattle.
 
• The festival marks the end of winter, and the beginning of the suns northward journey.
 
 
 
• **Bihu:**
 
 
• Bihu is a set of three important Assamese festivals in the Indian state of Assam.
 
• Rongali Bihu, also called Bohag Bihu, is the Assamese New Year, celebrated in mid-April.
 
• It marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year and the spring season.
 
• The festival involves traditional dances, music, and feasting.
 
• It is a very colorful festival that brings the entire community together.

• On this day, community guardians and environmentalists join together to celebrate their love for nature via a festival that recognizes what wetlands have done for not only humans but all living things.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Ramsar Convention **on Internationally Significant Wetlands Waterfowl Habitat is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands, which is particularly important.
 
• It's also known as the Wetlands Convention. It takes its name from the Iranian city of Ramsar, where the treaty was signed in **1971**.
 
• Representatives of the contracting parties gather every three years at the Conference of the Contracting Parties (COP), the convention's policy-making organ, to adopt decisions (resolutions and recommendations) to administer the convention's activities and strengthen the parties' ability to achieve its goals.

questions.question: In which year did the Bhopal gas tragedy occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1984**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• Bhopal Gas Tragedy:

 
 
• It happened on December 3, 1984.
 
• It was happened due to leakage of Methyl Isocyanate (CH3NCO) from the pesticide plant of Union Carbide (now Dow Chemicals), an MNC, in Madhya Pradesh capital Bhopal.
 
• It is estimated that about 40 tonnes of gas and other chemicals leaked from the Union Carbide factory.
 
• Methyl isocyanate is an extremely toxic gas and if its concentration in the air touches 21ppm (parts per million), it can cause death within minutes of inhaling the gas.
 
• It is one of the worst chemical disasters globally and still continues to have its ill effects on the people of the affected areas.
 
• After the tragedy, the government of India enacted a Public Liability Insurance Act (1991) that meant to provide immediate relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous industries. 
 
 
• Under the Act, an environment relief fund was set up to compensate affected people.

questions.question: The Republic Day parade, in the year 1955, was organised at which of the following places in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajpath**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Republic Day parade in 1955 was held at Rajpath in Delhi. **
 
• This **was the first time the parade was held in its present form at Rajpath**.
 
• Before 1955, **the parade was held at various venues, including Irwin Amphitheatre, Kingsway, Red Fort, and Ramlila Maidan**
 
• The first Republic Day parade was held on January 26, 1950.

• The inaugural Republic Day parade in India was a small gathering. The solemn ceremony took place in the nation's capital at the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, formerly known as the Irwin Amphitheatre.
 
• Dr Rajendra Prasad, India's first President, oversaw a ceremony to raise the flag.
 
• As the day the Indian National Congress (INC) issued the Declaration of Indian Independence in 1930, January 26 was chosen as India's Republic Day. The day was chosen since it was the day that the Poorna Swaraj resolution of the Congress was adopted.
 
• Republic Day is observed nationwide on January 26, 1950, the day the Constitution became operative. This day marked the beginning of India's ancient civilization, a mashup of several cultures and kingdoms. ​
